clue.text: Travel in France — US soldier getting cold is hypersensitive

parts.note: aller is the French verb meaning to go or travel
GI is the standard term for an American soldier
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone travelling around France meets an American soldier with a chill, and is touchy about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allergic means reacting excessively to a substance, the medical sense of hypersensitive.

clue.text: One impressed by false image, I had nothing subsequently

parts.note: contracted, I had becomes I'd
O looks like zero, nothing
subsequently means afterwards, later

explanation.surface: A confession: someone admired a false image, and afterwards had nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of idols is moved by a graven image, a false god in biblical terms.

clue.text: Traditions of border location?

definitions.meaning: established practices or habits handed down
the post at a frontier where goods are checked and duty paid

explanation.surface: A question about the traditions of a frontier region.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are traditional practices, and also the checkpoint at a national border where luggage is inspected.

clue.text: Sheds garments making journey aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on a vessel, so the journey word goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone undresses while taking a voyage on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off one's clothes, so a stripper sheds garments.

clue.text: English friend entering province of Asian country

indicators.note: entering signals that the English friend letters go inside the province letters

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An English friend arrives in a province of some Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is commonly called 'the Province' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali is the adjective for things belonging to Nepal, a Himalayan nation.

clue.text: Social difficulty with mum and boy meeting decent chaps taking time

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a lad is a boy
just means fair, decent
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A family with a mother and son has trouble getting along with respectable men, which takes a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladjustment is failure to adapt to one's social surroundings, a social difficulty.

clue.text: What could make remote wall rot in fort

indicators.note: could make suggests the given letters might be reworked into something else

explanation.surface: Asking what might turn a distant crumbling wall into a fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: A Martello tower is a small round coastal fort built in Britain during the Napoleonic Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Martello towers are small circular defensive forts built along coasts, so the answer is a kind of fort.

clue.text: See Cardiff install mostly new safety measure for pedestrians

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters
mostly means all but the last letter of install is used

explanation.surface: Cardiff is told to put in a new pedestrian safety feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims install to INSTAL, which joins CARDIFF for the anagram signalled by 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised refuge in the middle of a road lets people on foot cross in two stages, a safety measure.

clue.text: Author of 'Yellow Spring'

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Names the writer of a book apparently called Yellow Spring.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry 'or' is gold, the yellow tincture.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the English writer of Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Boat that's smart with name of island group

parts.note: trim means neat and smart
the Aran Islands are a group off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A smart vessel named after a cluster of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing vessel with three hulls side by side, a type of boat.

clue.text: Something disturbing? Notice nothing

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something upsetting happens, yet no one notices anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss and commotion, something that disturbs the peace.

clue.text: Burden beginning to worry crew

indicators.note: beginning to means take just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A burden starts to trouble the members of a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy load to bear, literally or as a responsibility.

clue.text: Dogs making row interrupting church service

indicators.note: interrupting means the row word breaks into the service word

parts.note: mass is the Catholic church service
a tiff is a minor quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: Dogs cause a commotion that disrupts a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a large, powerful breed of dog.

clue.text: Restriction that denies team a 24

definitions.meaning: a bond or constraint that limits freedom
a drawn match, in which neither side gains a victory (24 is the win)

explanation.surface: A restriction that stops a team from winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie can be a binding constraint, or a drawn game in which nobody gets the victory.

clue.text: Notice eccentric character at the end of short drama

indicators.note: at the end of places the eccentric after the shortened drama
short means the drama word loses its final letter

parts.note: a play is a drama
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: A notice goes up about an odd character appearing at the close of a brief play.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displaying a notice.

clue.text: Spring sees the uprising of a snake

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising lifts a letter higher up the column, towards the top

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Spring brings a snake rising up from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the uprising of a' moves the A of SPA to the top of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An asp is a small venomous snake, famous from Cleopatra's death.

clue.text: A crime rocking a country

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters of a crime into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal act shakes a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: America, the United States, is a country, and also a pair of continents.

clue.text: Twelve using power to restrict awful din

indicators.note: to restrict means the power word hems in the jumbled din

parts.note: might is power or strength

indicators.note: awful suggests the din is in a mess, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Twelve people use force to suppress a dreadful noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' looks like a number of people, but it is the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night.

clue.text: Californian can, maybe!

parts.note: can is US slang for a toilet; an American, such as a Californian, would call it by the polite euphemism for a public lavatory

explanation.surface: A tin can, perhaps from California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin, but it is American slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a public toilet is politely called by this name, and Californians are Americans.

clue.text: Fresh group of spectators in a stir once

parts.note: fresh means new
the gate is the crowd attending a sports match

explanation.surface: A new crowd of spectators once caused a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison, not a commotion; Newgate was London's notorious prison until 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a famous London jail, and stir is slang for prison, so it was a jail of former times.

clue.text: Dame's pet let loose, running out of control

indicators.note: let loose means the letters are freed to form a new order

explanation.surface: A lady's pet escapes and charges about wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a headlong rush of animals or people out of control.

clue.text: Jolly type from India diving into French river

indicators.note: diving into means the India letter plunges inside the river word

parts.note: the Marne is a river in France
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone from India jumps into a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Marines are nicknamed Jollies in British naval slang, so a jolly type is a soldier serving at sea.

clue.text: One wanting journalist's article travelled north to collect it

indicators.note: to collect means the reversed word gathers the it letters inside it
in a down clue going north reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone after a reporter's piece headed north to pick it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One wanting journalist's article' reads as an eager reader, but it is the person who commissions copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor commissions and awaits copy from the paper's writers.

clue.text: Stop rude sister needing wings clipped

indicators.note: clipping wings trims the outer letters at both ends of the phrase rude sister

explanation.surface: A demand that a rude sister calm down, with a jibe about trimming her wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing wings clipped' takes RU from the front and ER from the back of RUDESISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease doing something, a formal synonym for stop.

clue.text: Side no good — what it won't get?

indicators.note: no means the good letter is taken away from the side word

parts.note: a wing is a side, as of a building or a team's flank

explanation.surface: A useless team, and what it will never achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'Side no good': a hopeless team will not get a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor team will not achieve a victory, so a victory is what it won't get.

clue.text: Like bees in sun initially getting hot

indicators.note: initially means use only the opening letter of sun

parts.note: warming means becoming hot

explanation.surface: Bees out in the sunshine as things heat up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees fly in a dense moving mass, a swarm, so they are characteristically swarming.

clue.text: Attack route towards city centre, say?

definitions.meaning: an incursion or raid into territory
a street leading into town, read as two words

explanation.surface: An assault launched along the road into the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an advance or raid into enemy territory; split in two it is a road heading in.

clue.text: Our delight not wavering, giving end-of-year message

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Our joy stays firm, conveying a New Year greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: From Tennyson's In Memoriam, 'Ring out the old, ring in the new' is a traditional New Year sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from a Tennyson poem about bells marking the passing of the year, sent as a New Year sentiment.
